title: Pivot Decision — Do You Actually Need One?
body:
Before building a tunnel, answer one question: can Kali already reach the target directly? On PG Practice and OSCP labs, the VPN gateway often routes internal subnets for you — meaning you may have direct access to 'internal' machines without any pivot at all. Spending an hour fighting ligolo when the VPN already routes the subnet is the most common time waste in multi-machine labs.

The two-command test takes 10 seconds and definitively answers whether you need a pivot:

  1. ip route get <target-ip> — shows which interface and gateway would carry packets. 'dev tun0' means the VPN handles it. 'dev tunnel1' means your pivot handles it.
  2. nc -zv -w3 <target-ip> <port> — actually tries a TCP connection. 'Connection refused' means the host answered (reachable, port closed). 'Connection timed out' means routing failed or firewall dropped it.

Connection refused = routed correctly, port is just closed or filtered at the host level.
Connection timed out = not reachable — either no route or a firewall is dropping packets.

Do this test BEFORE setting up any tunnel. If the target is reachable over tun0, proceed directly. If it times out, then build the pivot.

The other confusion: when local admin or SYSTEM on a machine is not needed. On domain-joined boxes, the account's DOMAIN REACH matters more than local privesc. If you have domain credentials, test them against internal targets directly before grinding local privesc.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 1 — CHECK ROUTING (10 seconds, do this first)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
ip route get <target-ip>
# Output tells you everything:
# '<target> via 192.168.45.254 dev tun0'  → VPN routes it, no pivot needed
# '<target> dev tunnel1'                  → your pivot handles it
# 'Network unreachable'                   → no route at all, need pivot

# Show all routes to understand what's covered:
ip route show | grep -v 'linkdown'

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 2 — TEST ACTUAL CONNECTIVITY
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Pick a port you expect to be open (445, 80, 22, 5985):
nc -zv -w3 <target-ip> <port>
# 'Connection refused'  = HOST REACHABLE, port closed/filtered at host — no pivot needed
# 'Connection timed out' = NOT REACHABLE — need pivot or route is wrong
# 'Connected'           = Host reachable AND port open — proceed directly

# Quick multi-port check:
for port in 22 80 445 3389 5985; do nc -zv -w2 <target-ip> $port 2>&1; done

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STEP 3 — IF PIVOT IS NEEDED (timeout above)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Do you have a shell on a box that CAN reach the target?
# Check from that box:
# (Windows)  Test-NetConnection <target-ip> -Port 445
# (Linux)    nc -zv -w3 <target-ip> 445

# If yes — set up ligolo, chisel, or SSH tunnel from that box
# If no — find a different hop or re-examine the network topology

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FORCE TRAFFIC THROUGH A SPECIFIC INTERFACE
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Add a /32 host route (outranks any existing /24 — avoids 'File exists' error):
sudo ip route replace <target-ip>/32 dev tunnel1
ip route get <target-ip>    # verify: must now say 'dev tunnel1'

# Add a full subnet:
sudo ip route replace <subnet>/24 dev tunnel1

# Remove a route:
sudo ip route del <target-ip>/32
sudo ip route del <subnet>/24

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# DOMAIN REACH CHECK (no local SYSTEM needed)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# If you have domain creds, test them against internal targets FIRST:
netexec smb <internal-target> -u USER -p 'PASS'
netexec winrm <internal-target> -u USER -p 'PASS'
evil-winrm -i <internal-target> -u USER -p 'PASS'
# (Pwn3d!) = you already have access without any privesc on the current box

# From a Windows shell — test reachability to internal hosts:
Test-NetConnection <target-ip> -Port 5985
Test-NetConnection <target-ip> -Port 445
warn: 'Connection refused' and 'Connection timed out' mean completely different things. Refused = routed correctly, port is closed at the destination. Timeout = packets are not arriving at all (no route, or firewall dropping). Only timeout means you need a pivot. Also: ip route add throws 'RTNETLINK answers: File exists' if a route for that prefix already exists — use 'ip route replace' instead, which is idempotent.

choices.label: VPN routes it — no pivot needed, proceed directly
